body:
Reproducible on macOS with editor binary as well (when running project directly), so it's not specific to the export templates.

Trace (removed irrelevant platform specific frames):
```
MutexLock<MutexImpl<std::__1::recursive_mutex>>::MutexLock(MutexImpl<std::__1::recursive_mutex> const&) (core/os/mutex.h:77)
GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance() (modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2172)
GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance() (modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2171)
void memdelete<ScriptInstance>(ScriptInstance*) (core/os/memory.h:139)
Object::~Object() (core/object/object.cpp:2242)
RefCounted::~RefCounted() (core/object/ref_counted.h:52)
CoreBind::Logger::~Logger() (core/core_bind.h:123)
CoreBind::Logger::~Logger() (core/core_bind.h:123)
void memdelete<RefCounted>(RefCounted*) (core/os/memory.h:139)
Ref<CoreBind::Logger>::unref() (core/object/ref_counted.h:206)
Ref<CoreBind::Logger>::~Ref() (core/object/ref_counted.h:220)
Ref<CoreBind::Logger>::~Ref() (core/object/ref_counted.h:219)
void LocalVector<Ref<CoreBind::Logger>, unsigned int, false, false>::_resize<true>(unsigned int) (core/templates/local_vector.h:57)
LocalVector<Ref<CoreBind::Logger>, unsigned int, false, false>::resize(unsigned int) (core/templates/local_vector.h:184)
LocalVector<Ref<CoreBind::Logger>, unsigned int, false, false>::clear() (core/templates/local_vector.h:152)
CoreBind::OS::LoggerBind::clear() (core/core_bind.h:156)
CoreBind::OS::~OS() (core/core_bind.cpp:869)
CoreBind::OS::~OS() (core/core_bind.cpp:863)
void memdelete<CoreBind::OS>(CoreBind::OS*) (core/os/memory.h:139)
unregister_core_types() (core/register_core_types.cpp:414)
Main::cleanup(bool) (main/main.cpp:5121)
OS_MacOS_NSApp::cleanup() (platform/macos/os_macos.mm:1145)
...
OS_MacOS_NSApp::terminate() (platform/macos/os_macos.mm:1136)
...
OS_MacOS_NSApp::run() (platform/macos/os_macos.mm:1056)
main (platform/macos/godot_main_macos.mm:126)
```

Seems like `GDScriptLanguage` is uninitialized before loggers and `GDScriptLanguage::get_singleton()` (used in destructors) is null.

Tested and yes, calling `OS.remove_logger()` before exiting is a workaround. Not realiable though, since you don't really have destructors other than `NOTIFICATIONS` and they don't work the same on all platforms.
I can confirm this on 4.5.beta c81fd6c51 (Linux).
